explanatory_strength.rationale: The packet ties durable economics to a specific subscription mechanism: FY2025 free cash flow $9.85B ($23.07/sh), RPO $22.52B (65% within 12 months), Digital Media 95% gross margin, and workflow lock-in in Creative Cloud and Document Cloud. The distinguishing test is whether reinvestment and buybacks compound owner cash faster than generative-AI seat churn erodes pricing power; that test is stated with falsifiers but the moat is stable not widening and the reinvestment-return bridge is not hard-to-vary.

evidence_sufficiency.rationale: Core operating facts reconcile from full-tier FY2025 10-K and filing_facts (revenue $23.77B, OCF $10.03B, FCF $9.85B, 427M diluted shares, debt $6.21B). Five component proofs are mechanically complete with unique overlap keys. Decision-grade gaps remain: management_facts carries zero extracted claims; segment owner-cash split is a revenue-weighted approximation without filing-disclosed segment cash; the routed owner_earnings_reinvestment_dcf proof terminates at owner_cash_per_share × capitalization_multiple (28.8× on Digital Media) without reinvestment rate or incremental ROIC traces required by the quality_reinvestment route; Firefly ($0–$120/sh) and AI reserve (−$45 to −$5/sh) are widest judgment bands.

downside_control.rationale: Franchise downside is bounded by $9.85B recurring free cash flow, $22.52B RPO visibility, and an explicit AI competition reserve (base −$18/sh). Permanent loss is not structurally protected at $234.74: contract low case still implies 5.9% annualized return and equity remains exposed to multiple compression if net seat additions stall; $11.28B buybacks partly debt-funded (LT debt $6.21B, net cash −$779M) and $1.94B stock-based compensation dilutes economic ownership if repurchase pace slows.

return_vs_alternatives.rationale: Contract base annualized return 15.8% at $234.74 versus component base value $656/sh nominally clears a 12% owner-earnings hurdle, but the path depends on capitalization multiples (28.8× media, 23.4× experience) rather than traced reinvestment ROIC. Lawrence synthesis 32.0% is evidence_blocked and not decision-grade. Contract low 5.9% and high 22.9% bracket a base case sensitive to AI seat churn and multiple assumptions; capital deployment is watchable, not approvable on reinvestment proof alone.

claims.claim: Adobe is a durable subscription compounder within the quality_reinvestment power zone: filing-supported FY2025 owner cash $23.07/sh, 95% Digital Media gross margin, and RPO $22.52B support a pricing-power moat, though generative-AI competition keeps the advantage stable rather than widening.

FY2025 consolidated free cash flow $23.07/sh is the correct owner-cash anchor, but the contract proof applies revenue-weighted segment multiples instead of a reinvestment-rate and incremental-ROIC DCF, leaving the quality_reinvestment route's required reinvestment runway unproven.

At $234.74, contract base economics (15.8% annualized to $656/sh) are attractive on headline math but fail the Buffett/Weschler reinvestment-evidence bar; watch pending net seat cohort data and incremental ROIC on retained owner cash and buybacks.

strongest_counter_explanation: Generative-AI is an ARPU tailwind, not a moat threat: Firefly embedded in Creative Cloud converts AI demand into higher subscription tiers and credit monetization, RPO and H1 FY2026 revenue +12% prove seat retention, and the market correctly prices a widening workflow monopoly whose normalized owner cash will compound faster than the AI competition reserve assumes.
most_important_missing_fact: Filing- or management-disclosed net seat additions by cohort (individual vs enterprise) and generative-AI credit attach or utilization rates, needed to validate whether 9% Lawrence growth and 28.8× Digital Media capitalization embed sustainable reinvestment returns or peak-cycle optimism.
falsifiers: RPO growth falls below revenue growth for two consecutive quarters without offsetting ARPU lift disclosed in 10-Q filings.
Trailing four-quarter free cash flow per share falls below $18 for four quarters while buybacks stay above $8B annually.
Digital Media segment revenue growth decelerates below 5% year over year for two consecutive fiscal periods while stock-based compensation exceeds 8% of revenue.
specialist_findings: Within power zone (compounder, stable moat, partial dhando, in_power_zone true). Audited all five valuation-proof rows: digital_media_document_engine labels owner_earnings_reinvestment_dcf but proof is media_owner_cash_per_share ($17.13) × capitalization_multiple (28.8× base) = $493/sh with no reinvestment rate, incremental ROIC, or distributable-cash runway—fails route required_evidence; digital_experience_engine uses owner_cash_or_dividend_discount with experience_owner_cash ($5.69) × 23.4× = $133/sh; firefly_ai_monetization_option is judgment milestone ($50 base, $0–$120 band, non-overlapping); net_financial_claims filing-locked net debt ~−$1.82/sh, judgment base −$2/sh; ai_competition_and_sbc_reserve base −$18/sh separate from segment multiples. No comparables attached. Overlap controls pass (five unique keys, double_counting_flags empty). Option probabilities are judgment bands only. Capital requirement risk is multiple compression and SBC dilution, not insolvency. At $234.74 vs $656 contract base, annualized base return 15.8%; Lawrence 32.0% retained as migration reference only.
